_readme: Camera calibrations. ground.image: near-left, near-right, far-right, far-left corners of a rectangle on the road, picked at frame_size. width_m/length_m: that rectangle in metres; scale_verified=false means nobody measured it, so absolute metres and speeds are nominal (they cancel out of a wait only when the booth is in view). Lanes: across/along are fractions of the rectangle; along may run past [0,1]. booth_distance_m: metres from the strip's booth-end row to the inspection booth, null = not measured (no wait is produced, only queue and speed). cbp_lane: null until someone confirms which CBP lane type the strip is. mask: x,y,w,h overlays (clock, logos, QR codes, signs that hide the road). Check any change with `camera snapshot`. clock: the burned-in date/time box; a stream whose clock stops changing for 20 s is reported frozen.

pdn-north.title: Paso del Norte (Norte)
pdn-north.notes: Looks north up the bridge from the Juarez end; the US booths are past the far end, out of view. lane-1..lane-3 (left to right) split the carriageway between the yellow left curb and the white bollard line into equal thirds (width assumed 3 x 3.5 m). They are read separately because they queue separately: at 03:16 local on 2026-10-19 only the middle lane was queued. The lane between the bollards and the orange barrels, and the one right of them, are not calibrated yet. The Feliz Viaje sign hides the road behind it and is masked. lane-4 runs between the white bollards and the orange barrels, lane-5 between the barrels and the right curb; their edges were mapped through this rectangle's homography on a daylight frame (bollards at 1.00 of the width at every depth, curb 1.79-1.89, barrels tapering 1.45 to 1.25 where they end). At 08:40 local on 2026-10-19 the queue had moved from lanes 1-3 to these two.

lerdo-north.title: Lerdo (Norte)
lerdo-north.notes: Looks north along the Lerdo-Stanton bridge from the Juarez end. right-roadway is the straight stretch between the bollard line and the orange right curb, with the northbound arrow; width assumed two lanes (7 m). CBP names this port 'Stanton DCL', but which lane type the strip is has not been confirmed. Below y=380 the roadway curves left toward the camera and is not covered by the straight strip.

pdn-south-street.title: Paso del Norte (Sur)
pdn-south-street.notes: Looks south down the Juarez street that feeds the Paso del Norte bridge; the queue faces the camera and drives toward it, so the booth end is the near end and the bridge is behind the camera. No lane markings (cobblestone); the two strips follow the two queue columns seen at 04:56 local on 2026-10-19, left along the barrier fence. Vendors walk between the columns. Width assumed ~9 m.

bota-south-approach.title: CÃ³rdova - AmÃ©ricas (Sur)
bota-south-approach.notes: Looks south down the approach road to the Bridge of the Americas, with the bridge behind the camera. The queue in the left carriageway drives toward the camera: the reader's signed speed was negative in all 15 rounds from 03:16 to 07:56 local on 2026-10-19 with the booth set at the far end, so it is set at the near end. (Red lights seen on these cars at night had suggested the opposite; the measurement overruled that.) Two lanes, width assumed 7 m. The right carriageway carries other traffic and is not calibrated. BOTA is not administered by FPFCH (on-screen banner).

lerdo-south-booths.title: Lerdo (Sur)
lerdo-south-booths.notes: Lerdo, booths in the foreground: cars drive toward the camera and stop at gates staffed by uniformed officers, so the booth end is the near end and the booth is in view (booth_distance_m 0), which makes this the one calibration whose wait does not depend on its unverified scale. Direction is INFERRED as southbound (Mexican customs on arrival in Juarez) from the officers and the flow toward the Juarez end; not confirmed, hence direction_verified false. Two lanes split at the orange divider; width assumed 7 m.
